hints: You are not allowed extra memory, so no hash map. Is there an operation where combining a number with itself gives nothing, and the order of combining does not matter?
Use XOR: x ^ x = 0, x ^ 0 = x, and XOR is commutative. XOR all the numbers; every pair cancels and only the unpaired value remains.

1. x = 0.
  2. For each v in nums: x ^= v.
  3. Return x.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: For each element, count its occurrences with a second loop; return the one with count 1.

approaches.name: Better
approaches.idea: Count occurrences in a HashMap and return the key with count 1.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: XOR every value together; pairs cancel out.

explain: Sample [7,3,7]: 0 ^ 7 = 7, 7 ^ 3 = 4, 4 ^ 7 = 3. Order does not matter, so you can imagine the two 7s meeting and becoming 0, leaving 0 ^ 3 = 3. Negative numbers work the same way because XOR acts on the raw bits (sample 2 gives −1). Edge case: an array with one element just returns it.
recognize: 'Every value appears twice except one, O(1) space' → XOR everything.
javascript: function unpaired(nums) { const c = new Map(); for (const v of nums) c.set(v, (c.get(v) || 0) + 1); for (const [k, v] of c) if (v === 1) return k; }
